# Public Portuguese speech acceptance fixture

This is Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) test utterance `11247_10229_000002`, not user audio: a 12.46-second Brazilian Portuguese passage from the LibriVox recording of Graça Aranha's *Canaã* (speaker 11247, chapter 10229). MLS is distributed under **CC-BY-4.0**; credit: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve and Ronan Collobert, ["MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.03411), Interspeech 2020. The source recordings are LibriVox public-domain audio. [Corpus and license](https://www.openslr.org/94/), [CC-BY-4.0 terms](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

Source: the `portuguese` / `test` split of the [`facebook/multilingual_librispeech`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/facebook/multilingual_librispeech) dataset at revision `2e83e61823b4c47dcbcb1980bb88601274127609`, row 2, which the dataset serves as `11247_10229_000002.opus` (16 kHz mono Opus, SHA-256 `42f8d83544a7fe03b7fe9cbd39d4886d418fadca66d31f16f3f60d315cc02896`). `ffmpeg n9.0.2` decoded it to the included WAV (`-ac 1 -ar 16000 -c:a pcm_s16le`): no resampling, cropping or speech changes. The 398,798-byte WAV has SHA-256 `aaa5d3d1725c3a3c358c64ab6dbaf06b4c11ff8bbedafa55fd5e002c236c3d24`: mono 16 kHz signed 16-bit PCM (12.46 seconds). The Opus encoding is lossy, so the PCM is a decoded copy of that lossy stream, not the original LibriVox MP3.

`reference.txt` is the utterance's transcript from the dataset's `transcript` column (lower case, no punctuation), independent of Whisper's output. Acceptance uses word error rate against it with a threshold chosen from the multilingual tiny model's published limits, not tuned to a single run. One clean Brazilian Portuguese sample does not establish accuracy for other languages, accents, noisy microphones or device performance.
